Incision and drainage (Choice E) is not preferred over fine needle aspiration for the management of a refractory galactocele or breast abscess, as it is more invasive and has an increased rate of scarring and unfavorable cosmetic outcomes. Educational Objective: Galactoceles are retention cysts that form as a result of obstruction of a lactiferous duct that appear during lactation or shortly after cessation of lactation. Diagnosis of a galactocele is facilitated with mammography and ultrasonography. Treatment is primarily supportive with massage and application of heat, although patients with refractory symptoms may benefit from therapeutic fine needle aspiration. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A previously healthy 47-year-old woman comes to the physician 3 weeks after she noted a lump in her right breast during self-examination . Physical examination shows a 3-cm mass in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast. Mammography shows no abnormalities . Ultrasonography shows a cystic component ; fine-needle aspiration biopsy yields cloudy straw-colored fluid. The mass is still present after aspiration . Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
correctExplanation: Breast cancer encompasses many types of breast carcinoma, including invasive ductal and lobular carcinoma, medullary carcinoma, inflammatory breast carcinoma, and cystosarcoma phylloides. The most common type is invasive ductal carcinoma, which typically presents as a palpable, immobile breast mass, which may demonstrate features such as spiculated margins and microcalcifications on mammography. They can be associated with pathologic nipple discharge. Evaluation of a breast mass first involves imaging with either mammography, if over the age of 35 years, or ultrasonography, if under the age of 35 years to evaluate whether the palpable mass has features concerning for breast cancer. This is because younger women's breasts are denser and more challenging to evaluate with mammography than the breasts of older women. Mammography may be followed by ultrasonography. In this case, the mass persisted after ultrasonography-guided aspiration of fluid, indicating it is likely not a simple cyst. Therefore, it should be biopsied to rule out a breast malignancy. Biopsy is invasive and reserved for cases of moderate to increased clinical suspicion after investigation with diagnostic imaging takes place.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. Indefinite observation (Choice A), observation for 6 weeks (Choice B), or observation for 1 year (Choice C) are not appropriate management strategies. This mass has concerning features, namely the presence in a female over the age of 35 years and the persistence of the mass after aspiration, warranting urgent biopsy to rule out a breast carcinoma. Repeat mammography (Choice D) will not provide any new information about the diagnosis. Instead, biopsy is needed to definitively diagnose the pathology. Thermography (Choice E) is a screening test utilized in breast cancer that uses the body temperature of the skin and underlying soft tissues to identify the presence of a breast cancer. It is not used routinely as it has a false positive rate of 25% and a false negative rate of over 60%. Educational Objective: A breast mass with suspicious imaging features that demonstrates persistence after attempted aspiration is concerning for an underlying breast carcinoma. The next appropriate step in management is to conduct a core-needle or excisional biopsy to sample the lesion. This will allow a definitive diagnosis to be made. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A 32-year-old woman , gravida 4, para 3, at 38 weeks' gestation is admitted to the hospital 8 hours after premature rupture of membranes . Pregnancy had been uncomplicated . Previous pregnancies were uncomplicated with spontaneous vaginal delivery of 3430-g (7-lb 9-oz), 3629-g (8-lb), and 3770-g (8-lb 5-oz) newborns at 37 to 39 weeks' gestation . She has no history of serious illness . Her only medication is a prenatal vitamin . Her temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), pulse is 80/min , respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 112/65 mm Hg. The cervix is 1 cm dilated and 80% effaced . Labor augmentation with oxytocin is begun and results in contractions 2 to 3 minutes apart . The cervix is now 8 cm dilated and 100% effaced ; the vertex is at +2 station . Her temperature now is 39°C (102.2°F), pulse is 110/min, respirations are 22/min , and blood pressure is 105/58 mm Hg. The baseline fetal heart rate is 175/min with mild variable decelerations . The uterus is tender. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
correctExplanation: Chorioamnionitis is a polymicrobial bacterial infection of the fetal membranes and commonly occurs in premature or prolonged rupture of membranes because of the migration of vaginal flora into the uterus . Other risk factors include repeated digital vaginal examinations, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, and genital tract infections. Maternal fever and leukocytosis are characteristic, and the uterus may be tender to palpation with the presence of purulent amniotic fluid. Further evaluation of the amniotic fluid may disclose a positive Gram stain with culture, numerous leukocytes, and low glucose concentration. A fetal heart tracing would likely show tachycardia secondary to the maternal fever. Complications include uterine atony, wound infections, pelvic abscess, and sepsis. Treatment consists of delivery and intravenous antibiotics. As this patient is in active labor, with signs of appropriate cervical change, the addition of intravenous antibiotics and careful monitoring of labor progression are warranted.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. Increased oxytocin therapy (Choice B) is not necessary, as this patient has demonstrated adequate progression of labor on her current dose of oxytocin with contractions every 2 to 3 minutes and significant cervical change. Forceps delivery (Choice C) and vacuum extraction (Choice D) are often utilized for a prolonged second stage of labor or in the setting of fetal distress . They require a dilated and effaced cervix, ruptured membranes, and engaged occiput. As this patient is progressing appropriately through labor, assisted vaginal delivery is not necessary at this time. Immediate cesarean delivery (Choice E) is occasionally required in the setting of chorioamnionitis if there is evidence of fetal or maternal instability. However, this patient is progressing appropriately through the active stage of labor with no signs of fetal distress. Educational Objective: Chorioamnionitis is a polymicrobial infection of the fetal membranes that presents with fever, tender uterus, purulent amniotic fluid, and leukocytosis. Risk factors include prolonged or premature rupture of membranes. Treatment requires the administration of intravenous antibiotics and delivery. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A 67-year-old woman , gravida 3, para 3, comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of a rapidly increasing lower abdominal mass. Twenty years ago, she underwent radiation therapy of the pelvis for early cervical cancer; the uterus was not removed . She has been receiving estrogen and progesterone replacement therapy since then. She has smoked two packs of cigarettes daily for 40 years . Examination shows a normal-appearing vulva, vagina , and cervix . The uterus measures 16 cm. She undergoes exploratory laparotomy , total abdominal hysterectomy , and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy . Pathologic evaluation shows a uterine sarcoma . Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this pathologic finding?
correctExplanation: Uterine sarcoma is a rare malignant proliferation of the myometrium or the stroma of the uterus that most commonly occurs in postmenopausal women and typically presents with postmenopausal bleeding, abdominal pain, bloating, and a rapidly enlarging pelvic mass. Physical examination will disclose an enlarged uterus, and ultrasonography will show a heterogeneous mass with possible foci of internal necrosis. Typical evaluation includes an endometrial biopsy, as well as a biopsy of the mass itself, while treatment involves a total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, as well as lymph node dissection, and neoadjuvant chemotherapy depending on the extent of disease. Risk factors for the development of uterine sarcoma include pelvic radiation therapy, a history of retinoblastoma, and long-term use of tamoxifen.
incorrectExplanation: nd D. Cigarette smoking (Choice A) increases the risk for lung, urothelial, pancreatic, and squamous cell cancers (eg, skin, cervical, anal). It does not increase the risk for uterine sarcoma. Excessive estrogen (Choice B) plays a role in the development of endometrial hyperplasia and endometrial carcinoma because of its proliferative effect on the endometrium. This risk is decreased when used concomitantly with progesterone. Genetic predisposition (Choice C) can increase the risk for uterine sarcoma in the case of childhood retinoblastoma and the rare syndrome of hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer. This patient is otherwise healthy with the exception of her history of cervical cancer. Human papillomavirus infection (Choice D) is a sexually transmitted viral infection that can cause cervical, vulvar, penile, or anal carcinoma, as well as condylomata acuminata. It does not increase the risk for uterine sarcoma. Educational Objective: Uterine sarcoma presents with a rapidly enlarging pelvic mass, abdominal pain, postmenopausal bleeding, and an enlarged uterus. Risk factors include a history of pelvic radiation, retinoblastoma, and long-term use of tamoxifen. r O , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A healthy 27-year-old woman , gravida 3, para 2, at 32 weeks' gestation comes to the physician for a routine prenatal visit. She says that she feels well and has not had any uterine contractions . She reports that the baby has been very active . The patient has had a 1-kg (2-lb) weight gain since her last visit 2 weeks ago. She does not drink alcohol and quit smoking after she learned she was pregnant. She works as a bartender . Her blood pressure is 120/70 mm Hg. Examination shows a fundal height of 28 cm. Fetal heart tones are 150/min. Leopold maneuvers confirm a cephalic presentation . Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
correctExplanation: Fundal height is often used to estimate gestational age. The distance in centimeters between the pubic symphysis and top of the uterine fundus approximates the gestational age in weeks. Typically, gestational age is calculated from the last menstrual period. When there is a discrepancy between these two measurements, the most appropriate next step in management is ultrasonography to assess the fetus through objective parameters for accurate dating or to assess for discrepancies in fetal size. Measurements of the fetal crown-rump length, biparietal diameter, femur length, and abdominal circumference can be used to accurately date a pregnancy. Ultrasonography-guided gestational age measurements are the most accurate during the first trimester. Ultrasonography can also determine other causes for a fundal height smaller than expected, such as intrauterine growth restriction, or larger than expected, including multiple gestations, hydatidiform moles, and fetal macrosomia. In this case, the patient is likely experiencing intrauterine growth restriction, which can be secondary to uteroplacental insufficiency, congenital infections, or maternal substance use.
incorrectExplanation: nd F. Follow-up visit in 2 weeks (Choice A) would be appropriate if this patient had a healthy gestation at 36 weeks. However, as this fetus is potentially experiencing intrauterine growth restriction, performing ultrasonography is pertinent to confirm the diagnosis. Induction of labor (Choice C) is typically done with oxytocin in the setting of post-term pregnancy, medical complications of pregnancy (eg, eclampsia, chorioamnionitis), and fetal growth restriction. However, prior to inducing labor, it is important to confirm the diagnosis of intrauterine growth restriction. Percutaneous umbilical blood sampling (Choice D) is useful in the confirmation of severe fetal anemia and can offer additional diagnostic information on chromosomal or other fetal abnormalities if amniocentesis or chorionic villus sampling are nondiagnostic. However, it is invasive and carries the risk for fetal bleeding, fetomaternal bleeding, infection, and fetal loss. Amniocentesis (Choice E) is an invasive sampling of amniotic fluid through the abdominal wall, usually performed at 15 to 20 weeks' gestation, to evaluate for chromosomal or genetic abnormalities. While it may be useful in determining the cause of intrauterine growth restriction, the diagnosis should first be confirmed with ultrasonography. Cesarean delivery (Choice F) is the operative delivery of the fetus through the abdominal wall and is typically done in the setting of fetal malpresentation, macrosomia, placenta previa, and arrest of the active stage of labor. It plays less of a role in the management of intrauterine growth restriction. Educational Objective: Fundal height and gestational age discrepancies should be evaluated with fetal ultrasonography. Measurements of the fetal crown-rump length, biparietal diameter, femur length, and abdominal circumference can be used to accurately date a pregnancy. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A 32-year-old woman comes to the physician for a follow-up examination 4 months after beginning a trial of oral contraceptive therapy for menometrorrhagia . Her symptoms have improved . Menses now occur at regular 28- to 30-day intervals and last 3 days . Her last menstrual period was 2 weeks ago. She is otherwise healthy and takes no other medications . Physical examination , including pelvic examination , shows no abnormalities . Which of the following is the most likely explanation for the improvement in this patient's bleeding?

choices.A: Enhanced progesterone secretion by the corpus luteum

correctExplanation: Menometrorrhagia can be caused by a variety of structural abnormalities, systemic disorders, and endocrine dysfunction, such as leiomyomas or polyps, coagulopathies, and anovulatory cycles. It is defined by abnormally heavy menstrual periods that occur irregularly. Evaluation involves pelvic examination and ultrasonography. It can be treated with combined oral contraceptives, a progesterone intrauterine device, high­ dose oral progesterone therapy, or surgical resection depending on the underlying pathology. In this case, the combined oral contraceptives minimized the patient's bleeding as they resynchronized the endometrium into a typical hormonal cycle. During menses, follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone (FSH and LH, respectively) concentrations increase and stimulate the developing follicle. The follicle produces estrogen, which leads to proliferation of the endometrium in preparation for implantation of a fertilized ovum. Following ovulation, the corpus luteum forms. The corpus luteum secretes progesterone to maintain the endometrial lining. If no implantation occurs, the corpus luteum degrades to the corpus albicans and estrogen and progesterone concentrations decrease, causing menstruation and minor increases in FSH and LH. Combined oral contraceptives prevent ovulation and provide progesterone and estrogen to maintain the endometrium, which is sloughed when the contraceptive is withdrawn during the placebo week, resulting in menses.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. Enhanced progesterone secretion by the corpus luteum (Choice A) would not occur, as the corpus luteum would be less likely to develop because of the suppression of ovulation by the combined oral contraceptives. The progesterone required for endometrium maintenance is provided by the oral contraceptive. Increased luteinizing hormone (LH) concentration (Choice B) would not occur, as LH is inhibited by increased concentrations of progesterone and estrogen with oral contraceptives. Suppression of uterine adenomyosis (Choice C) is not correct, as adenomyosis is a less likely cause of abnormal uterine bleeding in this patient. Adenomyosis describes the growth of endometrial glands within the myometrium, is commonly seen in multigravid women, and is associated with an enlarged uterus on physical examination. Thickening of the cervical mucus (Choice E) is caused by oral contraceptives as part of their mechanism of action. However, cervical mucus changes are unlikely to alter menstrual period flow and regularity. Educational Objective: Menometrorrhagia refers to excessive menstrual periods at irregular time intervals. Depending on the underlying cause, initial treatment is commonly with combined oral contraceptives, as they result in resynchronization of the endometrium, although it can also be treated with a progesterone IUD, high-dose oral progesterone therapy, and surgical resection if required. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A 66-year-old woman is admitted to the hospital because of a 2-day history of decreased level of consciousness and dyspnea . Two years ago, she was diagnosed with stage IV epithelial ovarian cancer. The patient initially responded to surgical debulking and chemotherapy , but she has not responded to the past three chemotherapy regimens . Her last CT scan of the abdomen showed an increase in peritoneal tumor burden . The patient does not have an advance directive . She appears thin and is in moderate respiratory distress . She is unconscious and does not respond to verbal stimuli. Her temperature is 37.7°C (99.9°F), pulse is 110/min, respirations are 24/min , and blood pressure is 80/50 mm Hg. Breathing is labored , and breath sounds are decreased in the lower lung fields bilaterally. Her serum CA 125 concentration is 1236 U/ml (N<35); 1 month ago, it was 247 U/ml . The physician requests a family meeting with her two daughters . Which of the following is the most appropriate initial statement by the physician?

choices.A: "Do you want your mother to be an organ donor ?"
choices.B: "What do you think is hai:ipening with your mottler?"
choices.C: "Who is in charge of making decisions about your mother 's care?"
choices.D: "Would you like your mother to be put on life support ?"
choices.E: "Your mother will not live through the night."

correctExplanation: Physicians should begin end-of-life discussions with open-ended questions to assess the understanding of patients or family members of the situation. The physician can then tailor further discussion to address the emotional needs or knowledge gaps of patients or family members. For example, some members of the family may not realize that this patient may die imminently and may require education from the physician or time to process this news before they can make decisions about their mother's care. Once the physician ensures all involved parties understand the gravity of the situation, the physician can begin a collaborative discussion about end-of-life decisions that honors the patient's and family's wishes.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. Initially informing the family members that their mother may die or require life support soon (Choices A, D, and E) may be shocking to family members who may not yet appreciate the gravity of the situation and preclude further effective discussion about end-of-life decisions. Further, the physician's focus should be on the patient and her family, who require the physician's medical acumen and emotional support, rather than the potential recipient of the patient's organs (Choice A). Determining who will make decisions for the patient (Choice C) is an important early step in end-of-life discussions. However, the physician should first assess family members' understanding, as they may not realize that their mother has likely lost her decision-making capacity permanently and may die soon. Educational Objective: Physicians should begin end-of-life discussions with open-ended questions to assess the understanding of patients or family members of the gravity of the situation. The physician can then tailor further discussion to address the emotional needs or knowledge gaps of patients or family members. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: An 82-year-old woman with dementia , Alzheimer type , is brought to the physician by her daughter because of blood on her underwear . The patient is confused and smells of urine. She is not oriented to place or time , but she knows her name. Pelvic examination shows severe vaginal atrophy. There is a 3-cm , tender laceration and an erythematous , edematous vaginal perinea! body. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these findings?
correctExplanation: This patient presents with perinea! erythema, vaginal bleeding, and a genital laceration most likely secondary to mechanical trauma from a sexual assault. Further, the odor of urine likely indicates neglect. Elder abuse, neglect, and mistreatment is common. Skin tears, lacerations, and bruises in unusual spots suggest elder abuse. Sexual abuse specifically may present with pain in the genital area, vaginal or rectal bleeding, and bruises or lacerations of the vulva or breasts. Elder abuse can exacerbate cognitive impairment and may explain this patient's confusion and incontinence. Elderly patients who demonstrate signs of abuse should be interviewed without their caregiver present. Physicians are mandated by many states to report abuse of vulnerable adults to protective agencies.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. An acute allergic reaction (Choice A) such as contact dermatitis of the vagina may present with erythema, pruritus, burning, or soreness. Lacerations and vaginal bleeding would be atypical. Vulvar lichen planus (Choice B) is an uncommon inflammatory condition of the vulvar skin. Patients may present with vulvar soreness, intense pruritus, and burning. The erosive form may demonstrate narrowing of the introitus and loss of the labia minora. This patient's vaginal bleeding and lacerations are inconsistent with vulvar lichen plan us. Squamous cell carcinoma in situ (Choice D) of the vulva would present with an often raised, pruritic lesion. Patients with squamous cell carcinoma would not demonstrate perinea! erythema, vaginal bleeding, and a genital laceration. Urinary incontinence (Choice E) could lead to vulvar erythema and skin peeling. Linear lacerations and vaginal bleeding would be atypical. Educational Objective: Sexual abuse of elderly patients may present with pain in the genital area, vaginal or rectal bleeding, and lacerations or bruises of the vulva or breasts. Physicians are mandated by many states to report abuse of vulnerable adults to protective agencies. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A 30-year-old woman comes to the physician for a routine pelvic examination . She has had multiple sex partners . Perianal examination shows two venereal warts . Cervical examination shows no abnormalities . A Pap smear shows epithelial cells with an irregular nuclear contour and a distinct halo around the nucleus with a dense outer rim of cytoplasm . Which of the following is the most likely cause of the cytologic abnormalities?
correctExplanation: Soft, pink, papillary lesions on the external genitalia are consistent with condyloma acuminata, genital warts associated with human papillomavirus (HPV) that can appear on the penis, vagina, vulva, and/or anal canal. Multiple sexual partners and the failure to use condoms during sexual intercourse are risk factors for their development. The most commonly implicated strains of HPV are 6 and 11, which both have low oncogenic potential. High-risk HPV strains include 16, 18, 31, and 33, which may also be present and indicate an increased risk for progression to cervical dysplasia and malignancy. In this case, virally infected cells, or koilocytes, are visible on Pap smear as cells with an irregular contour and a perinuclear halo with the chromatin pushed to the edges of the cell. Viral infection with HPV is the cause of the cytologic atypia seen in this case. In order to identify this atypia early, screening Pap smears are recommended every 3 years in women aged 21 to 29 years and every 5 years in conjunction with HPV co-testing (every three years if co-testing is not performed) in women aged 30 to 65 years. Abnormal Pap smear cytology results are most commonly evaluated by colposcopy, which allows for the visual assessment and biopsy of abnormal lesions.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. Infection with Chlamydia trachomatis (Choice A) classically presents with urethritis, dysuria, and urethral or vaginal discharge. However, it can also be asymptomatic. Complications include cervicitis, epididymitis, reactive arthritis, and pelvic inflammatory disease. Chlamydia trachomatis is a sexually transmitted infection like HPV, but it does not cause cytologic atypia. Infection with cytomegalovirus (Choice B) can cause primary infection in immunocompetent hosts with symptoms that are indistinguishable from those of Epstein-Barr infection (mononucleosis). Patients present with fevers, myalgias, and laboratory evidence of atypical lymphocytosis, often with abnormal liver enzymes. The cells present in this patient are HPV-infected koilocytes, however, not reactive lymphocytes. Infection with herpes simplex virus 2 (HSV-2) (Choice C) causes genital herpes, which present with painful vesicles and shallow erosions commonly accompanied by fever, chills, and inguinal lymphadenopathy. However, unlike HPV, HSV infection does not cause cytologic atypia to develop. Invasive cervical carcinoma (Choice E) is classically associated with infection from HPV high-risk strains 16, 18, 31, and 33. It presents indolently until advanced, locally invasive, or metastatic; vaginal bleeding or post-coital spotting may be the presenting symptom. It cannot be diagnosed on cytology alone, as invasion must be demonstrated on biopsy or excision. The findings on this Pap smear are consistent with atypia from active viral infection. Educational Objective: Soft, pink, papillary lesions on the external genitalia are consistent with condyloma acuminata, which are associated with low risk strains of HPV. High-risk strains of HPV can also infect the epithelial cells of the cervix, causing atypia and the formation of koilocytes. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: Three days after a moderately difficult forceps delivery, a 27-year-old woman , gravida 1, para 1, comes to the physician because of a 3-day history of numbness and tingling of the anterior lower right leg. She also has had buckling of the right knee when she attempts to walk. Epidural anesthesia was administered during labor. After 4 hours of pushing in stirrups during the second stage of labor, spinal anesthesia was administered for the forceps delivery. Examination shows decreased sensation along the anterior, anteromedial , and medial aspect of the right thigh , knee, and upper leg. There is some weakness of the quadriceps femoris muscle . Which of the following is the most likely explanation for these findings?

choices.E: Injury to the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve

correctExplanation: Nerve compression injuries are caused by prolonged pressure against a nerve fiber, which results in nerve ischemia and demyelination, which may or may not be reversible depending on the extent of ischemia. The most commonly injured nerves in the lithotomy position (with feet in stirrups) are the femoral nerve and the peroneal nerve. The femoral nerve can be compressed under the inguinal ligament when the hip is flexed greater than 90 degrees, which can lead to numbness of the anterior and medial aspects of the thigh, as well as weakness of the quadriceps muscle, as in this patient. Peroneal nerve injuries typically are caused by compression at the fibular head against the stirrup, leading to foot drop and numbness over the dorsal foot and lateral lower extremity. Recovery of the function of either nerve depends on the length of time that the nerve was exposed to ischemia, but physical therapy can be useful.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. Adverse effects of epidural anesthesia (Choice A) and spinal anesthesia (Choice B) included back pain, headache, hematoma formation, infection (eg, epidural abscess), urinary retention, hypotension, and neuropathy. However, the risk for neuropathy is low, and it would be more likely to present bilaterally and in the distribution of a dermatome instead of within the territory of an individual nerve. Injuries to the genitofemoral nerve (Choice D) and lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (Choice E) can occur during open pelvic surgeries, as they both run along the pelvic sidewall. Agenitofemoral nerve injury presents with numbness of the upper medial thigh and scrotum or labia, whereas lateral femoral cutaneous nerve injuries present with pain along the anterior and lateral aspects of the thigh. Educational Objective: Prolonged positioning with hips flexed greater than 90 degrees can lead to femoral nerve injury, which presents with numbness of the anterior and medial aspects of the thigh, as well as weakness of the quadriceps muscle. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A 28-year-old nulligravid woman has had increasingly severe pelvic pain and dyspareunia over the past 8 months ; during menses , the pain worsens and she has occasional episodes of diarrhea . Pelvic examination shows a normal vagina and cervix with no suspicious lesions. The uterus is normal-sized , retroverted , and fixed , and there is induration and nodularity of the posterior wall of the uterus and cul-de-sac . There are no palpable adnexal masses . Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic test?
correctExplanation: Endometriosis refers to the presence of endometrial tissue outside of the uterus, and classically presents with symptoms of dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, and dyschezia. On physical examination, signs of ectopic endometrial tissue and subsequent fibrosis include palpable nodularity of the posterior uterus and cul-de-sac along with fixation of the uterus to nearby structures making it immobile, as in this case. The standard for diagnosis is a diagnostic laparoscopy, which evaluates for endometriotic implant lesions on the peritoneum. Oral contraceptive therapy can be used for the treatment of endometriosis. Another potential treatment is danazol, which acts to prevent the ovary from secreting estradiol by acting as a synthetic androgen and partial androgen receptor agonist.
incorrectExplanation: nd D. Measurement of serum CA 125 concentration (Choice A) is typically performed if an ovarian malignancy is suspected. It is a poor screening test but can be used to monitor progression of the disease and response to therapies. It is not increased in endometriosis and thus is not used to confirm the diagnosis. Barium enema (Choice B) is useful for the evaluation of intraluminal large bowel gastrointestinal pathologies. This patient's symptoms are more suggestive of endometriosis than a primary gastrointestinal pathology. CT scan of the pelvis (Choice C) and MRI of the pelvis (Choice D) may be used to evaluate gynecologic pathologies after physical examination and ultrasonography have failed to provide the necessary information. While they may suggest the diagnosis, neither of these tests definitively confirms the diagnosis of endometriosis. Educational Objective: Endometriosis is caused by ectopic endometrial gland implantation. Dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, and dyschezia are classic symptoms. Diagnosis is achieved with laparoscopy to evaluate for endometrial implants on the peritoneum. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A previously healthy, asymptomatic 25-year-old woman comes to the physician for contraceptive advice . She takes no medications . Menses occur at regular 28-day intervals and last approximately 5 days. Her last menstrual period was 20 days ago . Pelvic examination shows a 5-cm mobile mass in the right adnexa ; the mass is moderately painful to palpation . Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
correctExplanation: The corpus luteum develops from the mature follicle after the egg has ovulated during the menstrual cycle. In some instances, the corpus luteum can form a cyst, which can potentially rupture. A ruptured corpus luteum cyst classically presents with unilateral pelvic or lower abdominal pain that is sudden in onset and severe, most commonly after sexual intercourse or other physical activity. Physical examination may show a unilateral adnexal mass, which may be tender. A pelvic ultrasonography will show a complex cystic mass or free fluid in the pelvis if ruptured, which may include hemorrhagic components (hemoperitoneum). Culdocentesis (rarely performed) typically produces serosanguinous fluid, as the corpus luteum is highly vascular. It is typically managed with observation and supportive therapy.
incorrectExplanation: nd I. Adenocarcinoma of the gastrointestinal tract (Choice A) typically presents with constipation or decreased caliber of stool, hematochezia or melena, and weight loss, as well as iron deficiency anemia caused by chronic blood loss. It is more common in older patients and would be less likely to present in an asymptomatic patient with an adnexal mass. Adenocarcinoma of the ovary (Choice B) is more common in postmenopausal women and classically presents late in its course with weight loss, abdominal discomfort, and bloating. A palpable pelvic mass is more likely a benign corpus luteum cyst in this young, asymptomatic patient. Distended urinary bladder (Choice C), if in the setting of urinary retention or bladder outlet obstruction, commonly presents with abdominal pain, decreased urinary output, and a palpable suprapubic mass on abdominal examination. Urinary retention most commonly occurs postoperatively, after removal of a Foley catheter, or following a spinal cord injury. Diverticulitis (Choice D) most commonly presents with left lower quadrant abdominal pain, diarrhea, fever, and tenderness to palpation in the left lower quadrant. It does not present with an adnexal mass. It can present with a palpable adnexal mass, although this is relatively uncommon given the limited area in which the fetus can develop prior to rupture. It is unlikely in this patient with a recent last menstrual period. Endometrioma (Choice F) is a cyst that is formed from ectopic endometrial tissue within the adnexa. Endometriosis commonly presents with dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, and dyschezia. Additionally, endometriomas are generally adherent to nearby structures, and would be less likely to be freely mobile on pelvic examination. Lymphoma (Choice H) presents with weight loss, fevers, and night sweats in the setting of lymphadenopathy, with additional symptoms based on tumor location. It does not typically present with a pelvic mass. questionStem: A 24-year-old primigravid woman at 12 weeks' gestation comes to the physician for her first prenatal visit. She has immune thrombocytopenic purpura and wants to know whether this condition will affect her baby. Examination shows a uterus consistent in size with a 12-week gestation . This patient's fetus is at increased risk for which of the following?
correctExplanation: Immune thrombocytopenia purpura (ITP) is caused by autoantibodies against platelet surface antigens, most commonly glycoprotein Gpllb/llla. It can be primary or secondary to a variety of disorders, such as HIV, hepatitis C infection, systemic lupus erythematosus, and chronic lymphocytic leukemia. It typically presents with thrombocytopenia, with platelet counts commonly less than 100,000/mm 3. Patients often present with petechiae, purpura, and mucosal bleeding (eg, epistaxis, vaginal bleeding, gastrointestinal bleeding), which may occasionally result in profound hemorrhage if severe. Laboratory studies are otherwise within reference ranges, but bone marrow biopsy often shows megakaryocyte hyperplasia. It can be treated with steroids and intravenous immunoglobulin but may require splenectomy in refractory cases. As the antibodies responsible for ITP are typically lgG antibodies, which can cross the placenta, the fetus is at risk for autoantibody-mediated destruction of its platelets.
incorrectExplanation: nd E. Chronic maternal anemia (Choice A) can be seen in the setting of iron deficiency, folic acid deficiency, vitamin B12 (cobalamin) deficiency, chronic systemic illness, and chronic blood loss. It is not a direct consequence of ITP unless the mother suffers from recurrent mucosal bleeding. Fetal renal infarction (Choice C) is rare, but if present could lead to fetal distress and possible fetal demise. This may result in associated renal failure, which would be expected to present as oligohydramnios and resultant pulmonary dysplasia (Potter sequence). However, renal infarction is not a known complication of ITP. Maternal hypertension causing uteroplacental insufficiency (Choice D) is a common complication of gestational hypertension and preeclampsia, which can lead to intrauterine growth restriction and fetal demise. However, ITP does not cause maternal hypertension. Placental infarction (Choice E) would cause severe uteroplacental insufficiency and potential fetal demise depending on the timing of infarction with regard to the gestational age and delivery. However, in the setting of ITP, placental bleeding would be more likely to occur than infarction. Educational Objective: Immune thrombocytopenia purpura (ITP) is caused by autoantibodies against platelet surface antigens, most commonly glycoproteins Gpllb/llla. The associated lgG antibodies of maternal ITP can cause immune-mediated destruction of fetal platelets by crossing the placenta. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous

questionStem: A 27-year-old woman , gravida 2, para 2, comes to the physician because she is concerned that she may be pregnant. She was sexually active with her husband 2 days ago, and they did not use contraception . She wants to prevent an unintended pregnancy . She is breast-feeding their 7-month-old infant. Menses occur at regular 28-day intervals . Her last menstrual period was 1 week ago. She has a 5-year history of migraines and a history of hepatitis B. She was treated for Chlamydia trachomatis infection at the age of 17 years . She takes no medications and has no known drug allergies . Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination , including pelvic examination , shows no abnormalities . A urine pregnancy test is negative . Which of the following is a contraindication for the use of levonorgestrel as emergency contraception in this patient?
correctExplanation: Emergency contraception can be used after intercourse to prevent a pregnancy from occurring, most commonly by altering ovulation or preventing ovum fertilization. Primary forms of emergency contraception include levonorgestrel, ulipristal, and the copper intrauterine device. Levonorgestrel prevents ovulation and can be taken up to 72 hours after intercourse, although it is less effective at preventing pregnancy than the other methods. It has no significant contraindications and is safe to use in breastfeeding women, making it an acceptable choice for the patient in this scenario. Adverse effects include nausea, irregular menstrual bleeding, lower abdominal pain, and fatigue. Ulipristal is an anti-progesterone that also prevents ovulation. It can be used up to 5 days after intercourse and has no significant contraindications. Adverse effects are like those for levonorgestrel. A copper intrauterine device is the most effective form of emergency contraception and its use can be continued for long term contraception. It is effective if placed within 5 days of intercourse and has few contraindications, with exceptions including active uterine infection or an underlying anatomic abnormality (eg, septate uterus). Adverse effects include abdominal cramping, vaginal bleeding, infection, and uterine perforation.
incorrectExplanation: nd D. Breastfeeding (Choice A) is not a contraindication to emergency contraceptives, although combined oral contraceptives are usually avoided in patients that are breastfeeding because of the risk for prolactin inhibition and impaired milk production. History of Chlamydia trachomatis infection (Choice B) plays no role in the choice of emergency contraceptive. However, active infections would preclude the use of the copper intrauterine device. History of hepatitis B (Choice C) is not a contraindication to levonorgestrel, although it is primarily metabolized in the liver. Hepatitis B can be sexually transmitted, but it does not affect the ability to use an emergency contraceptive. History of migraines (Choice D) commonly precludes the use of estrogen-based contraception but does not affect the ability to use levonorgestrel. Educational Objective: Levonorgestrel can be used up to 72 hours after intercourse as an emergency contraceptive. It does not have any significant contraindications. r " , ~ r-- r , Previous
